newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close nearly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close nearly unchanged.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed nearly unchanged on Wednesday with the market stabilising after adjusting to April's lower-than-expected consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 105.46
Volume including Makams was 172 million shekels.

"There was big demand for some of the CPI-linked bonds but most of them were unchanged. There was no significant change in the market and it is stabilising at these levels," said Ilan Doron at Solid Financial Markets.
Yields of long-term CPI-linked bonds were at 4.1 percent and at 4.2 percent on short-term CPI-linked bonds, he said.
"Big demand continued for unlinked bonds, especially Makams which had a high volume of 75 million shekels," Doron said.
"The bonds are already anticipating May's CPI which is foreseen to be around 0.9 percent," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
"If the (Bank of Israel governor) will lower interest rates (for June) it will be a small cut, around 0.3 percentage points which will not affect the market," the trader said.

April's 0.7 percent CPI rise was well below analysts' forecasts of about 1.1 percent. The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its interest rate, to 13.9 percent, at the end of February.

Dollar-linked bonds closed nearly unchanged with a negative trend which traders called a reaction to the uncertain state of the dollar worldwide. The shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar on Wednesday at 3.3880 shekels against 3.3910 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
